name: MonarchGauge
title: Gauge
summary: A half-circle meter for one reading against a scale: bands give the scale a meaning, a target is marked, and the value is written as text.
whenToUse: For one reading against a known scale where the bands matter: utilisation, a health score, a quota used.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task use MonarchProgress. For several quotas use MonarchUsageMeter. For a value over time use MonarchSparkline.
api: @Composable fun MonarchGauge(value: Double?, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double> = 0.0..100.0, bands: List<MonarchGaugeBand> = emptyList(), target: Double? = null, tone: MonarchTone? = null, indicator: MonarchGaugeIndicator = MonarchGaugeIndicator.Arc, size: MonarchGaugeSize = MonarchGaugeSize.Md, showRange: Boolean = true, label: String? = null, description: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, valueLabel: String? = null, noValueLabel: String? = null)
class MonarchGaugeBand(range: ClosedFloatingPointRange<Double>, tone: MonarchTone, label: String? = null)
enum class MonarchGaugeSize { Sm, Md, Lg }

options.name: value
options.description: The reading. null, or a value that is not finite, shows an empty track and a dash.

options.name: bands
options.description: Stretches of the scale with a tone and a name.

options.name: target
options.description: A target on the scale, marked with a tick and added to the spoken value.

options.name: tone
options.description: The color of the value. null takes the tone of the value's band, Neutral outside every band, or the accent without bands.

options.name: indicator
options.description: Arc fills the track to the value; Needle draws the bands on the track and points at the value.

options.name: showRange
options.description: Writes the ends of the scale under the dial.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label under the gauge and its spoken name. "Gauge" (monarch_gauge_name) is spoken without one.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes every number. The default is a number in the current locale.

states.name: with a value
states.description: The track is filled to the value (Arc) or a needle points at it (Needle); the value is written in or under the dial.

states.name: in a band
states.description: The arc takes the band's color and the band's name is written under the value.

states.name: no value
states.description: An empty track, a dash, and "No data" as the spoken value.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Drawn at the nearest end of the scale; the text shows the real value.

appearance: The track is the muted background. The value arc uses the solid color of its tone, the accent solid without bands, and the strong border color for neutral; bands use the solid color of their tone. The target tick and the needle use the default text color; the range, band name and description use muted text. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web draws its own SVG and exposes a meter role; here the dial is drawn on a Compose Canvas and the gauge is one element with a progress range and a state description, because Android has no meter role. The web size is a number of pixels and the thickness can be set; here there are three sizes and the thickness is 12% of the width, as on iOS. The web tone accent is a null tone here. With the Arc indicator the bands are drawn as a thin arc inside the track, not outside it as on the web, so the dial needs no extra room. The scale starts at the start edge, so the dial is mirrored in right-to-left layouts; the web one is not. Above font scale 1.3, and with a needle, the value is written under the dial instead of inside it.
accessibility: The gauge is one element. Its content description is the label, or "Gauge".
It exposes a progress range from the start to the end of the scale, with the value limited to the scale.
Its state description is the reading and the name of its band ("72, At risk"), or the reading and the range ("72 (from 0 to 100)"), followed by the target ("Target 80").
Without a value it reads "No data" and has no progress range.
The value and the band name are written as text, so the reading does not depend on the arc or its color.
Text scales with the font size; the dial keeps its size, and above font scale 1.3 the value moves under it so it is never clipped.
The change of the arc and the needle is animated with the Monarch motion spec, and immediate when animations are removed.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A range whose ends are equal is widened by one.
A value that is not finite is treated as no value.
A value exactly on the boundary of two bands belongs to the upper one; the end of the scale belongs to the band that reaches it.
A band without a label falls back to the range in the spoken value; give every band a label.
Bands that reach beyond the range are drawn up to its end.

examples.title: With bands
A ratio, small
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    value = 0.55,
    range = 0.0..1.0,
    size = MonarchGaugeSize.Sm,
    label = "Quota used",
    formatValue = { "${(it * 100).toInt()}%" },
)

examples.title: A needle
examples.code:
MonarchGauge(
    value = 40.0,
    bands = listOf(
        MonarchGaugeBand(0.0..50.0, MonarchTone.Danger, "Low"),
        MonarchGaugeBand(50.0..100.0, MonarchTone.Success, "Good"),
    ),
    indicator = MonarchGaugeIndicator.Needle,
    label = "Score",
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web formats the value with an Intl.NumberFormat option bag (unit percent, no decimals); the native gauge takes a formatValue closure, so the template writes the same text (76%) with a closure.
parityExceptions.convention: Locale-driven formatting is native: Swift and Kotlin format numbers in code, not with Intl options.
